cc.audit_issues_finding_shape:
Two divergent conventions observed:
- review-architecture-auditor.md (lines 120-155) and review-cross-artifact-auditor.md schema: {id, severity, category, summary, evidence[], recommended_resolution}. NFR-8 in the PRD prescribes adding {rule, target, divergence, next_action} — these are NOT in the current schema.
- KB-review-disciplines/references/severity-taxonomy.md: same shape but uses three severity values (critical / important / recommended) plus a separate category dimension (consistency / completeness / compliance / clarity / feasibility) — a different vocabulary entirely. The reviewer discipline applies to shared-document-reviewer (Gate 0/1); the auditor agents emit BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR/INFO.
Net: there are TWO finding-shape conventions in the codebase today (auditor-style and reviewer-style). The Research Plan's IN-002 calls this out; FR-1 / FR-4 / FR-5 / FR-9 / FR-10 all emit auditor-style severities per the PRD. The reviewer-style remains for shared-document-reviewer at Gate 0/1.
cc.severity_string_convention:
Three severity surfaces in the codebase, each with its own vocabulary:
1. **Auditor agents** (review-architecture-auditor, review-cross-artifact-auditor, auditing-mcp SKILL.md `Severity meanings (v2)`): BLOCKER / MAJOR / MINOR / NIT (auditing-mcp) and BLOCKER / MAJOR / MINOR / INFO (architecture/cross-artifact auditors). Slight divergence (NIT vs INFO).
2. **shared-document-reviewer + KB-review-disciplines/severity-taxonomy.md**: critical / important / recommended. Score-based verdict mapping (consistency / completeness scores → verdict).
3. **Phase Validators** (test-phase-validator-author, .claude/agents/test-phase-validator-author.md Phase 2 'Severity rules' section): blocking / warning / informational.

verdict_compute.py (auditing-cc-configs) bridges 1↔point-deduction: BLOCKER -12, MAJOR -5, MINOR -2, NIT -0.5, INFO 0. PRD FR-1/4/5/9/10 explicitly emit BLOCKER and MAJOR per AC text — the auditor vocabulary is the operative one for those findings. The PRD's FR-3 (PV invariants) interacts with vocabulary 3.
cc.Blocks_X_marker_grammar_OI_A5: GREP RESULT: only ONE occurrence of 'Blocks <stage>' grammar across all working/feature/*/codebase-analysis*.md AND research-plan*.md, in working/feature/devcontainer-mcp-provisioning-r1/codebase-analysis-report.md lines 198-202. The grammar there is `Blocks design-composition-completion.` / `Blocks design-cc-completion.` (period-terminated; the stage-name is hyphenated kebab-case suffixed with `-completion`). NO state-transition log entries match the Blocks-X grammar. NO agent prompts or skill bodies emit such markers. The grammar is APPRESENT-BUT-NEAR-ABSENT: it exists in exactly one prior feature run's discovery output and nowhere else. Per OI-A5 / A-5 assumption: the grammar is essentially absent in the broader corpus, so FR-9 establishes the canonical grammar rather than reconciling heterogeneity. Recommendation for Synthesis: treat the devcontainer-mcp-provisioning-r1 codebase-analysis-report.md syntax as the precedent (`Blocks <stage-slug>-completion.`) and standardize from there. The Research Plan's expectation of 'heterogeneous OR absent' should be recorded as 'effectively absent (n=1 prior occurrence)'.
